body:
Changing a pod or a coil is the most frequent bit of maintenance a vape needs, and it is simple once you have done it a couple of times. Done well, it restores flavor and vapor at once and avoids leaks and burnt tastes. Done badly, it can leave you with a leaking device, a burnt new coil or a part that does not fit. This guide explains when to change, what you need, how to change a closed pod, a refillable pod, a tank coil and a disposable (which you cannot change), how to prime and fill, how to test, how to avoid common mistakes, how to dispose of old parts and how to build a routine. It is written for adults aged 21 and over. Nicotine is addictive, and nothing here is medical advice.

## When to change
Change a pod or coil when flavor fades, vapor thins, a burnt taste appears or the pod is empty. Do not wait until it is completely dry or burnt. As a guide, pods and coils last from several days to a few weeks. See [how often to replace coils](/blog/how-often-to-replace-coils/) and [vape flavor fading fixes](/blog/vape-flavor-fading-fixes/).

## What you need
- **The right replacement part,** matching your exact device. See [how to pick replacement coils and pods](/blog/how-to-pick-replacement-coils-and-pods/).
- **E-liquid,** for refillable pods and tanks.
- **Paper towels and dry cotton buds.**
- **A clean, flat surface.**

Wash your hands, and avoid touching the cotton or the heating element.

## Changing a closed pod
1. Switch the device off, if it has a power switch.
2. Remove the old pod by pulling it gently from the battery. Do not twist unless the design requires it.
3. Wipe the battery contacts with a dry cotton bud, and check the seat for liquid.
4. Unpack the new pod, and check that it is the right one.
5. Press the new pod in until it clicks. Do not force it.
6. Let it rest for a few minutes, so the wick soaks.
7. Take a few gentle puffs, then use as normal.

Dispose of the old pod responsibly; see [how to dispose of vapes and batteries](/blog/how-to-dispose-of-vapes-and-batteries/).

## Changing a refillable pod
1. Remove the pod from the device.
2. Empty any liquid and wipe the pod.
3. If the pod has a replaceable coil, remove the old coil and fit the new one. If the coil is built in, replace the pod.
4. Prime the new coil with a few drops of liquid.
5. Fill the pod below the max line, without splashing the center tube.
6. Seat the pod firmly.
7. Let it rest for five to ten minutes.
8. Take gentle puffs, then use as normal.

See [how to fill a pod without leaks](/blog/how-to-fill-a-pod-without-leaks/).

## Changing a tank coil
1. Switch the device off, and remove the tank.
2. Empty the tank, and wipe it.
3. Unscrew the old coil from the base, using the tank's design. Many unscrew by hand.
4. Check the base, threads and O-rings for residue, and clean them.
5. Unpack the new coil, and avoid touching the cotton.
6. Drip a few drops of liquid on the cotton through the wicking holes.
7. Screw the new coil in firmly, but do not overtighten.
8. Fill the tank below the line, and let it rest for five to ten minutes.
9. Start at the lower end of the coil's power range, with gentle puffs.

See [how to prime a new coil or pod](/blog/how-to-prime-a-new-coil-or-pod/) and [ohms, watts and volts](/blog/what-are-ohms-watts-and-volts-in-vaping/).

## Disposables
You cannot change the coil or pod in a disposable. It is a sealed device. When flavor fades and the liquid is finished, replace the whole device, and recycle the old one. Do not try to open it.

## Testing the new part
After the rest period, take two or three gentle puffs and check: does it fire, is the flavor right, is the vapor smooth and does it avoid gurgling or leaking? If it tastes burnt, rest it longer. If it leaks, check the seat and the fill level. If it does not fire, check the contacts and the connection. If problems continue, see [why a vape is not hitting](/blog/why-is-my-vape-not-hitting/).

## Fitting checks
- **The part is the right model.**
- **It seats fully,** with a click or a firm screw.
- **Contacts are clean and dry.**
- **O-rings are present and undamaged.**
- **The liquid level is below the line.**
- **Nothing is cross-threaded.**

## Common mistakes
- **Using the wrong part.**
- **Skipping priming.**
- **Overfilling.**
- **Overtightening threads.**
- **Touching the cotton.**
- **Firing the device before the coil has soaked.**
- **Leaving the old part in a bag with other items.**

## A worked example
Your tank has tasted flat for two days. You switch off, remove the tank and empty it. You unscrew the old coil, which looks dark and crusty. You wipe the base and replace a cracked O-ring. You drip six drops on the new coil's cotton, screw it in, fill the tank to the line and wait ten minutes. You set 28 watts, in the lower half of the range, and take gentle puffs. The flavor is back, bright and clean. You write the date on a sticky note, to track how long the coil lasts. The whole change takes about fifteen minutes, including the wait.

## Keeping a spare
Keep a spare pod or coil, primed if you wish, in a clean bag, upright, in a cool place. When you use it, order another. See [bulk buying tips](/blog/bulk-buying-vapes-save-money/) for planning stock. A spare turns a frustrating failure into a quick swap.

## Disposing of old parts
Old pods and coils contain residue and, in some pods, electronics. Keep them in a sealed bag out of reach of children and pets until you can take them to a hazardous waste or electronics recycling site, with your devices. Do not put them in household trash, and do not rinse them down the sink.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### How do I know a pod fits?
It seats firmly with a click, and the device recognizes it. If it does not, check the model. Do not force it.

### Can I reuse an old pod?
Refillable pods can be refilled until the coil wears out. Closed pods are not reusable.

### What if the new pod leaks?
Check the seat, the fill level and the seal. See [leaking causes and fixes](/blog/vape-leaking-causes-and-fixes/).

### Do I need to change the coil when I change flavor?
Not always, but strong residue can cause ghosting. Many users change the coil when moving to a very different flavor.

### How long does a changeover take?
About ten to fifteen minutes, including the soak.

## Shop
Browse [coils and pods](/shop/coils-pods/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## A changeover checklist
- Right part for the device, checked against the model name.
- Hands washed, surface clean.
- Old part removed gently.
- Contacts wiped dry.
- New part unpacked, cotton untouched.
- Coil primed with a few drops.
- Liquid filled below the line.
- Part seated firmly, threads not overtightened.
- Ten-minute rest.
- Gentle puffs, then normal use.
- Date noted for next change.

Print or save the list, and run through it each time. It takes a minute, and it prevents the usual mistakes.

## Changing in a hurry
If you must change a part when you are out, a closed pod is the easiest, because it needs no priming beyond a short rest. For a tank, carry a primed spare coil in a clean bag, so you can swap and refill. Do it in a clean place, with a paper towel, and keep liquid away from children and pets.

## Changing when it will not come out
If a pod or coil is stuck, do not force it. Check that it is the right model, that nothing is blocking it and that the release is correct. Try a gentle wiggle, and consult the manual. If it will not move, contact us with a photo and the model name. Forcing parts can break them.

## After the changeover
Check for leaks over the next few hours. Keep the device upright. If it gurgles, clear it as in [fixing a gurgling vape](/blog/vape-gurgling-sound-fix/). If flavor is not right, give the coil a day to settle, and check the liquid and settings. A new coil often tastes slightly different in the first few puffs, then improves.

## Frequently asked questions about changing parts
### How do I know when a pod is empty?
You may see liquid gone in the window, or flavor and vapor fade. Do not wait until it is dry.

### Can I change a coil while the tank is full?
It is better to empty the tank first, to avoid spills and flooding.

### Should I change pods and coils at the same time?
If the coil is built into the pod, yes. If separate, change the coil when it wears, and the pod when it cracks or is dirty.

### Can children or pets be near while I change parts?
Keep them away. Liquid and small parts can be hazardous.

### One more tip
Keep the packaging or a photo of the part for a day or two, so that if the new part is faulty you can show us exactly what you received. Contact us through the [contact page](/contact/) with your order ID if a part is faulty from new.

faq.q: How do I change a closed pod?
faq.a: Switch off, pull the old pod out, wipe the contacts, press the new pod in until it clicks, let it rest a few minutes and take gentle puffs.

faq.q: How do I change a tank coil?
faq.a: Empty the tank, unscrew the old coil, clean the base, prime the new coil, screw it in firmly, fill below the line, rest for five to ten minutes and start at low power.

faq.q: Can I change the coil in a disposable?
faq.a: No. Disposables are sealed. Replace the whole device when it is finished.

faq.q: Why must I prime a new coil?
faq.a: Dry cotton burns when heated, which spoils the coil. Soaking it first prevents that.

faq.q: What if the new coil tastes burnt?
faq.a: Rest it longer and use low power. If it persists, replace it and check the liquid and settings.

faq.q: How do I dispose of old parts?
faq.a: Seal them in a bag, keep them out of reach and take them to a hazardous waste or electronics recycling site.
